intro: Each row is a question that must be answered before a specific decision is reasonable. 'Known' is limited to what an official source in this repository establishes today. 'Unknown' is left blank on purpose. 'Fastest discovery' names the concrete action that would produce evidence - not a guess.

questions.question: Which official capture is the current source of truth for Week 10 availability?
questions.blocks: Every injury-driven signal, every availability feature and the completeness metric shown on the site.
questions.known: The published snapshot was captured 2026-11-12T06:32:36Z and holds 254 injury rows and 4 no-injury sections (VR-04, VR-07).
questions.discovery: Re-run the capture now, diff it row by row against the published snapshot, and publish whichever one matches the live page with its own timestamp. Then make capture age visible on every injury-derived page.

questions.question: How do we detect a silently truncated scrape before it is published?
questions.blocks: Trust in every table on the site. The four under-counted clubs (VR-13) and the two false no-injury sections (VR-05, VR-06) were published without any warning.
questions.known: Twenty of twenty-four published per-club counts matched the live report; the staged capture timestamp and the current page disagree, and no check compared them.
questions.discovery: Add a parse assertion that counts player rows per club section and fails the build when a club has zero rows but its section exists, or when the sum differs from a recorded expectation by more than zero. This is deterministic and needs no judgement.

questions.question: Does the capture pipeline distinguish 'no injuries reported' from 'no rows parsed'?
questions.blocks: Any claim that a team has no availability concerns.
questions.known: The pipeline can emit an explicit no-injury section from the page text, and it also emits zero rows when a table fails to parse. The two states reached the same rendered output for Seattle and Cincinnati.
questions.discovery: Separate the states in the data model (no_injury_reported vs not_captured) and render them differently, with a visible warning for not_captured.

questions.question: Which clubs publish a depth chart as an image rather than text, and how should that be handled?
questions.blocks: Backup-order coverage for those clubs, and the honest labelling of coverage gaps.
questions.known: Houston publishes the chart as an image with no player names in text (VR-15). Green Bay publishes a full text table and was wrongly reported as unparseable (VR-14).
questions.discovery: Probe each club page and classify: text table, image only, or absent. Record the classification with a timestamp instead of a generic parse error.
questions.source_label: Houston Texans club depth chart (image only)

questions.question: How is a replacement confirmed rather than inferred from a depth rank?
questions.blocks: The requested '2nd/3rd/4th string replacing a starter' deficiency metric.
questions.known: The weekly report lists status only. The NFL separately publishes announced starter changes: Drew Lock expected to start for Seattle (VR-24), Kyle McCord in line for a first start in Miami (VR-25), Jacoby Brissett acquired and installed in Baltimore (VR-17).
questions.discovery: Add an 'announced starter' evidence field populated only from dated NFL or club articles, kept separate from depth rank and from the injury report. Never derive it from rank arithmetic.
questions.source_label: NFL: Darnold ruled out, Lock expected to start

questions.question: Is absence from the weekly injury report evidence that a player is available?
questions.blocks: Any availability model that reads 'not listed' as 'healthy'.
questions.known: Malik Willis does not appear on the Week 10 injury report and is on injured reserve, ineligible until Dec 13 (VR-25).
questions.discovery: Capture the official reserve list and transactions pages alongside the weekly report, and encode 'not listed' as unknown rather than available.

questions.question: What do we do when a club chart is stale relative to transactions?
questions.blocks: Depth-based features for clubs with a recent quarterback or line change.
questions.known: Baltimore's published chart still lists Lamar Jackson first and Tyler Huntley second; the live chart now lists Brissett, Fagnano and Slovis (VR-17), consistent with the Nov 5 IR moves and the Nov 6 trade.
questions.discovery: Join each depth capture to the official transactions log by date; when a listed player has a later transaction, mark the row stale instead of silently publishing it.

questions.question: How are two players sharing one published slot represented?
questions.blocks: Any numeric ranking or dropoff calculation that assumes one player per rank.
questions.known: Seattle lists Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed inside the same first-string WR cell (VR-23); Washington leaves an empty second slot between Frankie Luvu and Kain Medrano (VR-21).
questions.discovery: Model a slot as a set plus an explicit empty-slot token, and render shared slots as shared. Validate by player name, never by row count.

questions.question: Which clubs were on bye, and should their absence be reported as a gap?
questions.blocks: Coverage reporting; a by-week club looks like a data failure when it is not.
questions.known: The Week 10 schedule lists Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay on bye (VR-16); these are exactly the four depth-only clubs.
questions.discovery: Capture the official schedule and annotate bye clubs so coverage differences have a cause instead of an alarm.
questions.source_label: NFL Week 10 schedule and bye list

questions.question: What permissioned market history is required before an originated line can be scored?
questions.blocks: Line origination, closing-line value, ROI, parlay pricing and the leaderboard itself.
questions.known: The NFL serves odds from FanDuel, Caesars and DraftKings through partner widgets and redirects betting to the bookmaker; it does not publish a historical price archive (VR-28).
questions.discovery: Obtain written terms for historical prices, timestamps, limits and redistribution from at least one provider. Until then, keep all market cells blank.

questions.question: What settles a bet, and which official page proves it?
questions.blocks: Any accuracy, ROI or leaderboard score.
questions.known: Official NFL game pages and schedules carry final scores and status; settlement rules (pushes, voids, stat corrections) are bookmaker terms, not NFL content.
questions.discovery: Define a settlement contract per market, name the official source for each field, and store the bookmaker rule reference separately from the NFL fact.
questions.source_label: NFL official schedule (game identity and kickoff)

questions.question: What is the minimum honest sample for a personnel-dropoff signal?
questions.blocks: Claiming that a 2nd- or 3rd-string replacement measurably changes performance.
questions.known: The tooling already requires at least 256 graded games, 2 seasons, 3 folds and 128 shadow games before a strategy can be ranked; uncertainty widens as the sample shrinks (VR-30).
questions.discovery: Pre-register the threshold before looking at results, then run the ablation. Do not tune the threshold to make a result appear.
questions.source_label: NIST/SEMATECH confidence limits for the mean

questions.question: How do we stop combo and prop research from leaking across a game?
questions.blocks: Any parlay or player-prop combination result.
questions.known: Time-ordered splitting prevents training on future data (VR-29); legs from the same game are not independent samples and need game-level grouping.
questions.discovery: Group folds by game and by week, and require matched joint outcomes for every leg before computing a combo probability.

questions.question: Which tracking metrics are defensible for a personnel signal?
questions.blocks: Replacing coverage or separation assumptions with real measurement.
questions.known: Next Gen Stats defines Completion Probability, Expected Completion Percentage, Aggressiveness (defender within 1 yard), Average Separation and Cushion (VR-31). None of these are captured in this repository.
questions.discovery: Determine whether any authorised tracking feed is obtainable at all; if not, restrict the signal set to official box-score fields and say so on the page.

questions.question: Who is the audience, and are stakes ever handled?
questions.blocks: Whether any of this may be published as advice, and whether rewards may be paid.
questions.known: The site is static, collects no accounts and states it is research-only; no reward funding or legal review exists.
questions.discovery: Answer in writing before any reward or advice feature. Default stays analytics-only and recognition-only.
questions.source_label: NFL Support: widget boundary and bookmaker redirect

questions.question: How does a live re-check become repeatable instead of a one-off manual pass?
questions.blocks: Confidence that the published tables still match their sources next week.
questions.known: This pass re-checked 32 claims by opening each source; the CI gates check structure and local links only and cannot see a stale or truncated capture.
questions.discovery: Record an expected value with each verified claim, then diff live captures against it on a schedule and publish the diff. Turn each confirmed structural defect into a regression test.
